old_entry.title: Horizon Zero Dawn
old_entry.subtitle: Hunting the Future in the Ruins of the Past
old_entry.summary: Horizon Zero Dawn introduced Aloy, an outcast trying to understand her own past in a world inhabited by animal-like machines.
body: Horizon Zero Dawn introduced Aloy, an outcast trying to understand her own past in a world inhabited by animal-like machines. Guerrilla's 2017 action role-playing game set tribal settlements beside the remains of a much older technological civilisation. The two histories are connected, although their relationship is initially unclear.

Aloy's Focus helps her examine machines, and her weapons let her approach encounters with different preparations. Learning what a machine carries and how it moves can matter more than repeatedly striking its largest surface. Hunting becomes a sequence of observation, a chosen tool and a response to what changes.

The Focus can also recover recordings from ancient ruins. These fragments connect a place the player explores with people who once used it. The same device that helps Aloy read an immediate threat therefore helps her investigate the larger question of what happened to the world.

old_entry.title: Call of Duty: Warzone
old_entry.subtitle: Verdansk Turns Call of Duty into a Shared Space
old_entry.summary: Call of Duty: Warzone launched in March 2020 as a free-to-play game from Infinity Ward and Raven Software.
body: Call of Duty: Warzone launched in March 2020 as a free-to-play game from Infinity Ward and Raven Software. At launch, up to 150 players entered Verdansk in teams of three. It supported crossplay, allowing the same match to bring together friends using PlayStation 4, Xbox One and PC.

The Gulag gave an eliminated player a one-on-one fight for a chance to return. Teammates could also spend in-match cash at Buy Stations to recover a fallen squad member. These systems made a defeat something the squad could respond to, instead of always ending that person's participation immediately.

Cash paid for equipment and other advantages, while optional Contracts offered rewards for taking on another task. Plunder made collecting cash the central goal and allowed repeated respawns. The two launch modes used the same broad environment to produce different reasons to move, take a risk or help a teammate.

In the Plunder mode, teams have to search for stacks of Cash scattered around the map to accumulate $1 million. Once found or if time is almost up, the game goes into overtime, multiplying all Cash sums by 1.5. The team who has gathered the most money when the clock runs out is declared the winner. Players respawn automatically in this gamemode. Players spawn with custom loadouts, similar to regular multiplayer modes.

original.old_heading: Verdansk Turns Call of Duty into a Shared Space
original.old_body: Call of Duty: Warzone enters this calendar through concrete design choices rather than through anniversary alone. Recognizable elements such as Verdansk, Gulag, Buy Stations connect online space and the presence of others with long-term service and continuous change. In 2020, those choices organize rules, production and presentation into an experience the player has to read while acting. That movement from intention to play is what makes the subject historically useful: systems, characters, technology and cultural context stop behaving like separate categories and begin to reinforce one another. The chapters that follow start from specific, verifiable details and trace their consequences, asking how Call of Duty: Warzone established its identity and which parts of that identity continued to influence the medium afterward.
